fx.backtestTitle: Track record · {model} vs the naive model
fx.backtestLead: {n} forecasts per horizon since {from}, each made only with data available on its date. “vs naive” below 1.00 means better than assuming the rate does not move.
fx.backtestNoEdge: No model beats naive on the point value today; their value is the range, which adapts to current volatility.
fx.noForecast: No forecasts published yet. Run: fxworkers forecast run.
fx.model.ewma_vol.name: EWMA volatility
fx.model.ewma_vol.description: Point = last FIX; range width starts at EWMA(0.94) volatility and relaxes toward 5-year volatility (φ = 0.97), so ranges widen quickly in turbulent markets.
fx.model.naive.name: Naive (random walk)
fx.model.naive.description: Benchmark. Point = last FIX; ranges from past moves of the same length over 5 years.
fx.pointFlat: This model's point is today's FIX at every horizon; the table shows how the range widens.
fx.forwardNote: The forward is today's price to lock in the rate for that date: it comes from the gap between TIIE and US Treasury rates. It is not a prediction; historically it missed by more than assuming the rate does not move (see below).
fx.model.forward.name: Market forward
fx.model.forward.description: Point = FIX × (1 + TIIE·d/360) / (1 + US Treasury·d/365), tenor interpolated between published rates; range = EWMA volatility band around the forward.
